# Transformer Attention & Scaled Dot-Product Attention

## The Intuition

In a sequence (e.g., a sentence), each token's meaning depends on the *other* tokens. Attention lets every position "look at" every other position and build a context-dependent representation. The core question is:

> *"How much should token *i* pay attention to token *j*?"*

The answer is encoded in a weighted sum over all positions, where the weights come from how relevant (similar) each pair of tokens is.

## The Three Matrices

| Name | Role | Shape (per head) |
|------|------|-----------------|
| **Q** (Query) | "What am I looking for?" | `(batch, seq, d_k)` |
| **K** (Key) | "What do I contain?" | `(batch, seq, d_k)` |
| **V** (Value) | "What information do I offer?" | `(batch, seq, d_v)` |

Q and K live in the same space (`d_k` dims) so we can measure relevance via dot product. V lives in a (possibly different) space (`d_v`) that carries the actual content to be aggregated.

## The Formula

$$\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V$$
